questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Force applied per unit area is termed :

solution.concept: 6.1 Pressure is the force acting per unit area
steps: Pressure = force ÷ area
Its unit is N/m², the pascal

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Observe the given distance-time graph. The distance covered by the train at 9:30 AM is :

solution.concept: 8.3 & 8.4 Speed from a distance-time graph
steps: The straight line shows uniform motion: 50 km every hour from 6:00 AM (200 km at 10:00)
At 9:30 the train has run 3½ hours: 50 × 3.5 = 175 km

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt:
Four electromagnets and the length of insulated wire used to make them are given in the table below.
The strongest electromagnet among these is :

solution.concept: 4.1 Electromagnets: more turns of the coil make a stronger electromagnet
steps: With the same core, a longer wire makes more turns
Q uses the longest wire (154 cm), so it is the strongest

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The nature of a shiny surface in relation to the reflection of light is :

options.A: More reflection, less absorption, less scattering
options.B: Less reflection, more absorption, more scattering
options.C: More reflection, less absorption, more scattering
options.D: Less reflection, more absorption, less scattering

solution.concept: 11.5 Reflection of light: shiny surfaces reflect most of the light falling on them
steps: A shiny, smooth surface reflects most light in one direction (like a mirror)
So it has more reflection, less absorption and less scattering

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt:
Read the given statements and choose the correct alternative.
Statement 1 : A person can skate easily over the skating ground.
Statement 2 : The frictional force of the ground is greater than the muscular force of the person.

options.B: Statement 1 is false and 2 is true
options.C: Statement 1 is true and 2 is false

solution.concept: 5.4.1 Friction is less on smooth surfaces
steps: Statement 1: a skating ground is smooth, so a person skates easily: true
Statement 2: easy skating means friction is small, less than the person’s muscular force: false

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Which one of the following statements about friction is true?

options.A: Friction increases as surface irregularities increase
options.B: Friction increases as surface regularities increase
options.C: Friction increases as surface irregularities decrease
options.D: Friction decreases as surface regularities decrease

solution.concept: 5.4.1 Friction is caused by the irregularities of the two surfaces locking together
steps: More irregularities (a rougher surface) lock together more
So friction increases as surface irregularities increase

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: An object of mass 1 kg is thrown upward with a force of 2 N. If the force applied is doubled in the same direction, then the object :

options.B: Continues to move further in the upward direction
options.C: Tends to move in the opposite direction
options.D: Stops moving, as the mass is doubled

solution.concept: 5.1 & 5.2 A force in the direction of motion increases the speed
steps: Doubling the upward force pushes the object harder in the same direction
So it moves further upward; its direction does not change, and its mass stays the same
Note: a 1 kg object weighs about 10 N, so a real 2 N or 4 N push could not lift it; the paper means only that a bigger force in the same direction carries it further

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The reason for designing an aeroplane in the shape of a bird is to :

solution.concept: 5.4.1 Fluid friction (drag): streamlined shapes cut it down
steps: Air resists an aeroplane moving through it
A streamlined, bird-like shape reduces this fluid friction

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt:
In the given diagram, four points L, M, N, O represent four taps that are connected at different heights.
The right order of the water pressure in these taps is :

solution.concept: 6.1 Liquid pressure increases with depth
steps: From the top of the tank down, the taps are O, M, N and L
The deeper the tap, the higher the pressure: O < M < N < L

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt:
Observe the given list.
i. Plastered floor
ii. Cement road
iii. Vacuum
iv. Polished metal
The decreasing order of frictional force in these is :

solution.concept: 5.4.1 Friction depends on the roughness of the surfaces in contact
steps: Cement road (roughest) > plastered floor > polished metal (smooth)
In a vacuum there is no surface to rub against, so the least friction: ii, i, iv, iii

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt:
A student tries to fix an iron nail into a wall by hammering on the sharp point of the nail, as shown in the diagram below.
The correct conclusion is :

options.A: He fails, as the surface area increases and the pressure decreases.
options.B: He succeeds, as the surface area decreases and the pressure increases.
options.C: He succeeds, as the surface area increases and the pressure decreases.
options.D: He fails, as the surface area decreases and the pressure increases.

solution.concept: 6.1 Pressure = force ÷ area: a smaller area gives a higher pressure
steps: Hammering on the point pushes the broad head against the wall
The area touching the wall is large, so the pressure is low and the nail does not go in: he fails

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt:
Observe the events given here.
i. Gravitational force between the Sun and the Moon
ii. Weathering of rocks
iii. Light travelling in vacuum
iv. Planets orbiting around the Sun
The events that remain unaffected by friction are :

solution.concept: 5.4.1 Friction acts only where surfaces (or fluids) rub against each other
steps: Gravity between the Sun and the Moon, light in a vacuum and planets orbiting through space involve no rubbing surfaces: i, iii, iv
Weathering of rocks involves rubbing by wind, water and sand, so friction plays a part

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt:
Observe the natural resources given below.
i. Coal
ii. Sunlight
iii. Natural gas
iv. Air
The resources which are not likely to be exhausted by human activities are :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Coal and Petroleum: inexhaustible and exhaustible resources
steps: Sunlight (ii) and air (iv) are present in unlimited amounts: inexhaustible
Coal and natural gas are fossil fuels and will run out

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: A bike is burning as its petrol tank has caught fire. The suitable fire extinguisher and the reason for your choice are :

options.A: Water – reduces the ignition temperature of the fuel
options.B: Blanket – increases the supply of carbon dioxide
options.C: Sand – extinguishes the fire by supplying more oxygen
options.D: Carbon dioxide – cuts off contact between the fuel and oxygen

solution.concept: 5.3.2 Fire triangle: take away fuel, oxygen or heat and the fire goes out
steps: Carbon dioxide is heavier than air and covers the burning petrol like a blanket
It cuts off the oxygen, so the fire goes out
Water is wrong for a petrol fire: petrol floats on it and keeps burning

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: It is advised to stop building thermal power plants in future, because by this :

options.B: Use of natural gas can be increased
options.C: The risk of increased global warming can be minimised
options.D: More coal gas can be used in vehicles

solution.concept: 13.6 Climate change: burning fossil fuels releases greenhouse gases
steps: Thermal power plants burn coal and release a lot of carbon dioxide
Building fewer of them limits the rise in global warming

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: A candle produces a flame while burning, because :

options.A: Molten wax vaporises by rising through the wick
options.B: The flame produced burns with the help of air
options.C: Wax reacts with oxygen to form the flame
options.D: Wax reacts with air as it is combustible

solution.concept: 5.4 Burning of a candle: the wax vapour is what burns
steps: Wax melts, rises up the wick and turns into vapour (physical changes)
The wax vapour burns in air with a flame (chemical change); substances that vaporise as they burn give a flame
Solid wax does not burn by itself, so C and D miss the step that makes the flame

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: When we are stung by a honey bee, we first wash the area with water and then apply baking soda, because water :

options.A: acts as a base and baking soda produces salt
options.B: reduces the acid and baking soda dilutes it
options.C: dilutes the acid and baking soda neutralises it
options.D: reduces the base and baking soda oxidises it

solution.concept: 2.3 Neutralisation in daily life: a mild base treats an acidic sting
steps: A bee sting puts an acid into the skin
Washing with water dilutes the acid, and baking soda (a mild base) neutralises the rest

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt:
Observe the statements given about liquefied petroleum gas.
i. It doesn’t burn easily in air.
ii. It produces a large amount of heat.
iii. It has a higher calorific value.
The correct option, which marks the statements true (T) and false (F), is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Combustion and Flame: LPG is a good fuel
steps: i. LPG catches fire very easily: F
ii. It gives a large amount of heat: T; iii. it has a high calorific value: T

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Observe the experimental set-up given here. The method to test the released gas is :

options.A: When tested with a burning candle, it burns more brightly
options.B: When passed through lime water, it turns milky
options.C: When put into distilled water, the colour turns brown
options.D: When tested with a burning candle, it burns with a ‘pop’ sound

solution.concept: 5.3 Lemon juice (or vinegar) + baking soda gives carbon dioxide, which turns lime water milky
steps: The gas from lime juice and baking soda is carbon dioxide
Passed through lime water it turns it milky (calcium carbonate forms)
A brighter flame would be oxygen and a ‘pop’ would be hydrogen

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt:
Observe the following statements about fossil fuels.
i. They were formed from the dead remains of organisms.
ii. Coal and petroleum are the only fossil fuels.
iii. Burning them is a major cause of air pollution.
iv. They are inexhaustible resources.
The right statements are :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Coal and Petroleum: fossil fuels
steps: i. They formed from the dead remains of organisms: true; iii. burning them pollutes the air: true
ii. Natural gas is a fossil fuel too, so false; iv. they are exhaustible, so false

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The gas released by the incomplete combustion of fossil fuels :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Combustion and Flame: incomplete combustion gives carbon monoxide
steps: When there is not enough air, carbon in the fuel burns only to carbon monoxide (CO), a poisonous gas
Complete combustion gives carbon dioxide instead

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The group of substances manufactured from petrochemicals among the following :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Coal and Petroleum: petrochemicals
steps: Polyester, polythene and detergents are made from petrochemicals, and urea from the hydrogen in natural gas
Each other option has an item that is not: steel, soaps (from fats) or naphthalene (from coal tar)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt:
Read the following statements and choose the correct alternative.
Assertion : People in rural parts of our country should reduce the use of wood as fuel.
Reason : Using wood as fuel produces more smoke and leads to deforestation.

options.A: Both assertion and reason are true
options.B: Assertion is true but the reason is false
options.C: Assertion is false but the reason is true
options.D: Both assertion and reason are false

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Combustion and Flame: wood is a poor fuel
steps: Burning wood gives a lot of smoke, which harms health, and cutting trees for fuel causes deforestation
So rural people should use less wood: both the assertion and the reason are true

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: A useful micro-organism found in the root nodules of the toor plant is :

solution.concept: 2.4.2 Rhizobium lives in the root nodules of leguminous plants
steps: Toor (pigeon pea) is a pulse, a legume
Its root nodules hold Rhizobium, which fixes nitrogen

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt:
Observe the statements about the sprinkler irrigation system.
i. Advantageous for land with insufficient water.
ii. Useful for lawns.
iii. A good method for uneven land.
iv. Suitable for watering gardens and trees.
The right option is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Crop Production and Management: sprinkler irrigation
steps: Sprinklers suit land short of water (i), lawns (ii) and uneven land (iii)
Gardens and trees are best watered drop by drop with drip irrigation, so iv is left out

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt:
Assertion (A) : 2,4-D should be used very carefully.
Reason (R) : Being a weedicide, it has ill effects on health.

options.A: Both ‘A’ and ‘R’ are true but ‘R’ is not the correct explanation of ‘A’
options.B: Both ‘A’ and ‘R’ are true and ‘R’ is the correct explanation of ‘A’

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Crop Production and Management: weedicides
steps: 2,4-D is a weedicide sprayed to kill weeds
It can harm the health of farmers, so it must be used carefully: both true, and R explains A

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Farmers of North Karnataka grow toor in one season and jowar in the next season. The main objective of this method is :

options.A: To get food crops for daily use
options.B: To balance the availability of water
options.C: To replenish nitrogen in the soil
options.D: To protect the crops from insects

solution.concept: 2.4.2 Crop rotation with legumes puts nitrogen back into the soil
steps: Toor is a legume; the Rhizobium in its root nodules fixes nitrogen
The jowar sown next uses that nitrogen, with less need for fertiliser

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt:
Agricultural scientists suggest that farmers should not use too many chemical fertilisers. The reasons for this are that they :
i. are the main source of water pollution.
ii. destroy soil fertility.
iii. kill useful micro-organisms.
iv. make the soil porous.
The right option is :

solution.concept: 12.7–12.9 Sustainable agriculture: too much chemical fertiliser harms the soil
steps: Fertiliser washed from fields pollutes water (i), lowers soil fertility (ii) and kills useful soil microbes (iii)
It does not make the soil porous (iv); manure improves soil texture

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: The micro-organism used for making medicine among the following :

solution.concept: 3.5.1 Antibiotics: Fleming got penicillin from the mould Penicillium
steps: The medicine penicillin is made from Penicillium
Amoeba and Paramecium are protozoa; bread mould is not used for medicines

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Identify the micro-organism in this diagram.

solution.concept: 2.3 Moulds: bread mould (Rhizopus) is a multicellular fungus
steps: The picture shows thread-like hyphae with round, dotted spore cases on upright stalks and root-like threads below
That is bread mould (Rhizopus); Penicillium has brush-like tips, Amoeba is a single cell, and Spirogyra is a green ribbon-like alga

questions.subject: biology

solution.concept: 2.4.2 Lactobacillus turns milk into curd and ferments batters

Added curd makes the rava idli batter ferment and turn sour

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Sodium benzoate is added while preparing pickles because it is a :

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Match the scientists and their discoveries and choose the correct alternative.

options.A: i – a, ii – b, iii – c, iv – d
options.B: i – b, ii – a, iii – c, iv – d
options.C: i – b, ii – d, iii – a, iv – c
options.D: i – c, ii – d, iii – a, iv – b

solution.concept: 3.5 Vaccines and antibiotics: Jenner made the smallpox vaccine and Fleming discovered penicillin
steps: Jenner – smallpox vaccine (ii – d); Fleming – penicillin (iv – c)
Pasteur – fermentation (i – b); Koch – Bacillus anthracis (iii – a)

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Observe the diagram of the heart given here. The name, structure and function of the labelled part ‘X’ is :

options.A: Aorta, thick elastic wall, carries blood from the heart
options.B: Vein, thick elastic wall, carries blood from the heart
options.C: Aorta, thin wall, carries blood from the body to the heart
options.D: Vein, thin wall, carries blood from the body to the heart

solution.concept: 9.2.1 Circulatory system: the heart pumps blood through blood vessels to every cell
steps: X is the large arched vessel leaving the top of the heart: the aorta
It carries blood from the heart to the body under high pressure, so its wall is thick and elastic
Veins have thin walls and bring blood back to the heart

questions.subject: biology

solution.concept: 13.5.2 Parts of a flower: the stamens (male) and the pistil (female)

Cucumber has separate male and female flowers; mustard, rose and hibiscus flowers have both parts

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: Among the following, the curve that is simple but not closed is :

solution.concept: Curves: a simple curve does not cross itself; a closed curve ends where it starts

options.B: Every integer is a whole number.

Interior angle = 180° − 45° = 135°

In a rhombus, in general :
i. All sides are equal

iii. The diagonals bisect each other at right angles
iv. Adjacent angles are supplementary

questions.prompt: The numbers from 10 to 20 are written on different cards (one number on each card), mixed well and kept in a box. One card is picked from the box without looking. The probability of getting a prime number is :

solution.concept: Probability = number of favourable outcomes ÷ number of all outcomes
steps: Cards 10 to 20: 20 − 10 + 1 = 11 cards
Primes among them: 11, 13, 17, 19 (4 cards)
Probability = 4/11

questions.prompt: The least number to be subtracted from 775 to make it a perfect square is :

solution.concept: 1.1 Estimating square roots: find the squares just below and above the number
steps: 27² = 729 and 28² = 784, so 729 is the largest square below 775
